title: The kindness of strangers
titleChinese: 有感于陌生人的慈善心怀
paragraphs: How much empathy do you feel towards other people? If you saw someone fall off their bike in traffic, would you stop and help - or just walk away? Many people would give in to apathy, go about their business and just do nothing. So it was a big surprise when about 100 bystanders got together recently to move a bus in east London to help a cyclist trapped under it. A video of the incident went viral on social media.

According to Zoheb, a driver who stopped his car to take part in the rescue, about five people gathered to move the bus. He says: "There was no chance we could do it, it was more an invitation for other people to help, really".
The initiative paid off. Diners from nearby restaurants joined in. There wasn't much coordination but it didn't take long to develop a collective understanding of what the objective was.

Spontaneous collaboration among strangers doesn't happen often. People in a crowd are not sure what to do - they don't have a plan. It's one of the reasons bystanders often do nothing, according to... Dr Mark Levine, professor of social psychology at Exeter University in Britain. "The presence of others can inhibit you from helping", he says.

The key to positive group behaviour and intervention, Levine explains, "is building a sense of shared identity". Action has to be decided quickly, Levine says. "The longer you leave it, the harder it is to make a decision. If you don't immediately act then you kind of think 'Well, actually I probably couldn't have done anything anyway'."
But the people who took the initiative like Zoheb might make a difference. The cyclist ended up in hospital and the images of the collective effort might inspire others to more acts of solidarity.

vocabulary.entry: empathy /ˈempəθi/ n. 同理心；共情
vocabulary.example: Empathy helps us understand other people's feelings.
vocabulary.translation: 同理心帮助我们理解他人的感受。

vocabulary.entry: give in to /ɡɪv ɪn tuː/ 屈服于；放任（情绪）（短语）
vocabulary.example: Don't give in to apathy when others are in need.
vocabulary.translation: 当他人陷入困境时，不要变得冷漠。

vocabulary.entry: apathy /ˈæpəθi/ n. 冷漠；漠然
vocabulary.example: Public apathy can lead to many social problems.
vocabulary.translation: 公众的冷漠会引发诸多社会问题。

vocabulary.entry: go about their business /ɡəʊ əˈbaʊt ðeə ˈbɪznəs/ 自顾行事；埋头做自己的事（短语）
vocabulary.example: Most people go about their business and ignore strangers' trouble.
vocabulary.translation: 大多数人只顾自己，无视陌生人的困境。

vocabulary.entry: bystander /ˈbaɪstændə(r)/ n. 旁观者；路人
vocabulary.example: Kind bystanders stepped forward to save the injured man.
vocabulary.translation: 善良的路人主动上前救助伤者。

vocabulary.entry: cyclist /ˈsaɪklɪst/ n. 骑行者；骑自行车的人
vocabulary.example: The injured cyclist was sent to hospital at once.
vocabulary.translation: 受伤的骑行者立刻被送往医院。

vocabulary.entry: trap /træp/ v. 困住；使陷入
vocabulary.example: The man was trapped under the large bus.
vocabulary.translation: 这名男子被困在大型公交车下方。

vocabulary.entry: go viral /ɡəʊ ˈvaɪrəl/ 走红；全网疯传（短语）（口语词汇）
vocabulary.example: The warm rescue video went viral online.
vocabulary.translation: 这段暖心的救援视频在网上爆红。

vocabulary.entry: take part in /teɪk pɑːt ɪn/ 参与；加入（短语）
vocabulary.example: Many citizens took part in the voluntary rescue.
vocabulary.translation: 许多市民参与了这场自发救援。

vocabulary.entry: initiative /ɪˈnɪʃətɪv/ n. 倡议；主动行动
vocabulary.example: His small initiative changed the whole situation.
vocabulary.translation: 他小小的主动举动改变了全局。

vocabulary.entry: pay off /peɪ ɒf/ 奏效；取得成效（短语）
vocabulary.example: Their joint efforts finally paid off.
vocabulary.translation: 他们的共同努力最终有了成效。

vocabulary.entry: join in /dʒɔɪ ɪn/ 加入；一同参与（短语）
vocabulary.example: Passers-by joined in to lift the heavy vehicle.
vocabulary.translation: 路人纷纷加入，合力抬起沉重的车辆。

vocabulary.entry: coordination /kəʊˌɔːdɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 协调；配合
vocabulary.example: Good coordination improves group efficiency.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的配合能提升团队效率。

vocabulary.entry: collective /kəˈlektɪv/ adj. 集体的；共同的
vocabulary.example: Collective strength can solve difficult problems.
vocabulary.translation: 集体的力量可以攻克难题。

vocabulary.entry: objective /əbˈdʒektɪv/ n. 目标；目的
vocabulary.example: Our main objective was to free the trapped person.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的首要目标是解救被困人员。

vocabulary.entry: spontaneous /spɒnˈteɪniəs/ adj. 自发的；即兴的
vocabulary.example: It was a spontaneous act of kindness from strangers.
vocabulary.translation: 这是陌生人一次自发的善意举动。

vocabulary.entry: collaboration /kəˌlæbəˈreɪʃn/ n. 协作；合作
vocabulary.example: Close collaboration saved a person's life.
vocabulary.translation: 紧密的协作挽救了一条生命。

vocabulary.entry: inhibit /ɪnˈhɪbɪt/ v. 抑制；阻碍
vocabulary.example: Inner worries can inhibit people from helping others.
vocabulary.translation: 内心的顾虑会阻碍人们伸出援手。

vocabulary.entry: intervention /ˌɪntəˈvenʃn/ n. 介入；干预
vocabulary.example: Timely intervention can reduce unnecessary harm.
vocabulary.translation: 及时介入能够减少不必要的伤害。

vocabulary.entry: shared identity /ʃeə aɪˈdentəti/ 共同身份认同感（短语）
vocabulary.example: Shared identity unites people in difficult moments.
vocabulary.translation: 共同的认同感能在困境中凝聚人心。

vocabulary.entry: take the initiative /teɪk ði ɪˈnɪʃətɪv/ 主动带头；采取主动（短语）
vocabulary.example: He took the initiative to start the rescue work.
vocabulary.translation: 他主动带头开展救援工作。

vocabulary.entry: make a difference /meɪk ə ˈdɪfrəns/ 产生影响；有所作为（短语）（口语词汇）
vocabulary.example: One person's action can make a great difference.
vocabulary.translation: 一个人的行动也能带来巨大改变。

vocabulary.entry: end up /end ʌp/ 最终处于；到头来（短语）
vocabulary.example: He ended up receiving good treatment in hospital.
vocabulary.translation: 他最终在医院得到了良好的救治。

vocabulary.entry: solidarity /ˌsɒlɪˈdærəti/ n. 团结；互帮互助
vocabulary.example: The event shows the power of social solidarity.
vocabulary.translation: 这件事展现了社会团结的力量。

sentences.chinese: 你对他人有多少同情心哪？

sentences.chinese: 如果你看到有人在车流中从自行车上摔下来，你会停下来帮忙，还是直接走开？

sentences.chinese: 许多人会选择冷漠，忙于自己的事，什么也不做。

sentences.english: A video of the incident went viral on social media.
sentences.chinese: 这一事件的视频在社交媒体上疯传。

sentences.english: According to Zoheb, a driver who stopped his car to take part in the rescue, about five people gathered to move the bus.
sentences.chinese: 据参与救援的司机佐赫布（Zoheb）说，最初大约有五个人聚集在一起来移动公交车。

sentences.chinese: 他说：“我们不可能做到，这更像是邀请其他人来提供帮助。”

sentences.english: The initiative paid off.
sentences.chinese: 这一倡议取得了成功。

sentences.english: Diners from nearby restaurants joined in.

sentences.english: There wasn't much coordination but it didn't take long to develop a collective understanding of what the objective was.
sentences.chinese: 虽然没有太多协调，但人们很快就全部理解了什么是行动目标。

sentences.english: Spontaneous collaboration among strangers doesn't happen often.
sentences.chinese: 陌生人之间的自发合作并不常见。

sentences.chinese: 群体中的人们不确定该做什么——他们没有计划。

sentences.chinese: 英国埃克塞特大学社会心理学教授马克·莱文（Mark Levine）博士表示，这是旁观者经常什么都不做的原因之一。

sentences.chinese: 莱文解释说，积极的群体行为和干预的关键是“建立一种共同的身份认同感”。

sentences.english: Action has to be decided quickly, Levine says.
sentences.chinese: 他同时还说，必须迅速决定行动。

sentences.english: "The longer you leave it, the harder it is to make a decision.
sentences.chinese: “拖得越久，做决定就越难。

sentences.english: If you don't immediately act then you kind of think 'Well, actually I probably couldn't have done anything anyway'."
sentences.chinese: 如果你不立即采取行动，你可能就会想，‘嗯，其实我可能什么都做不了。’”

sentences.english: But the people who took the initiative like Zoheb might make a difference.
sentences.chinese: 但像佐赫布这样主动采取行动的人可能会带来改变。

sentences.english: The cyclist ended up in hospital and the images of the collective effort might inspire others to more acts of solidarity.
sentences.chinese: 骑自行车的人最终被送往医院，而集体努力的画面可能会激励其他人采取更多齐心协力的行动。
